title: Release sprint cadence and risk ops cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick operational reference for coordinating cross-functional release sprints that include canaries and A/B experiments. Intended as a lightweight, copyable checklist and cadence guide for PMs, Eng, SRE and CS during a staged rollout.

Context / assumptions:
- Target audience: product managers running model/console feature rollouts and SRE/ENG on-call.
- Platform: Redwood Console rollouts framework + Canary routing + A/B routing.
- Baseline: production release candidate has unit/e2e tests passing and perf benched locally.
- This is a working cheat sheet — copy it into a ticket (RI-xxxx) and adapt.

Quick glossary (short):
- Canary slice: small percentage of real traffic routed to new variant for early signals.
- Experiment cohort: A/B assignment for feature or model variant where we collect metrics.
- Guardrail: an automated check (alert/hold) that prevents further ramp.
- Roll-forward: increase traffic share; Rollback: revert to previous variant.

Pre-launch checklist (2–3 days before):
- [ ] Define hypothesis: what metric(s) will indicate success? (primary metric + 1–2 safety metrics).
  - Example: hypothesis: "Model v2 reduces median prompt latency by 15% without increasing hallucination rate."
- [ ] Owners assigned: PM, Eng lead, SRE on-call, Data analyst, CS lead.
- [ ] Create ticket with experiment matrix: cohorts, traffic slices, start/end windows, measurement queries. Link to ticket in Console rollout config.
- [ ] QA: smoke tests on staging that exercise typical prompt shapes and length distributions.
- [ ] Load sanity: run a small load test matching expected canary qps (e.g., 10–50rps) with KV cache warmup.
- [ ] Observability: ensure dashboards and alerts exist. Add temporary dashboards if needed.

Minimum telemetry (dashboards/panels to check):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 (p95_latency_ms) by route and model.
- Errors: 4xx/5xx counts and inferred model-failure indicators (error_rate_5m).
- Quality signals: downstream QA eval pass rate, closed-loop user complaints, regression test accuracy.
- Cost/throughput: token_cost_per_1000, inference_throughput_tps, GPU_util_percent.
- Backpressure: queue_length, request_dropped_count, kv_cache_hit_rate.

Automated guardrails (recommended thresholds - tune per product):
- Hold if p95_latency increases by >20% vs baseline for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Hold if error_rate_5m > 0.5% (absolute) or >3x baseline.
- Hold if token_cost_per_1000 increases > 25% and no quality gain observed.
- Hold if GPU_util_percent > 95% sustained for 1 minute.
- If any guardrail fires, auto-reduce slice to previous stable variant (or 0% if severe) and notify #prod-rollouts + on-call.

Example staged ramp plan (canary -> broad):
- Step 0: Internal dogfood / feature-team test (0.01% traffic or dedicated internal header). 1–2 hours.
- Step 1 (Canary A): 0.5% traffic, 30 minutes observation.
- Step 2 (Canary B): 2% traffic, 60 minutes observation.
- Step 3: 10% traffic, 2–6 hours (parallel checks on business metrics).
- Step 4: 50% traffic, 12–24 hours.
- Step 5: 100% rollout or convert to target experiment splits.
Notes: shorten or lengthen windows based on traffic volume. For low-volume routes, keep percent small and extend time window.

A/B experiment example (hypothesis and metrics):
- Hypothesis: directing 25% of users to compact model variant reduces cost by 40% while NPS remains unchanged.
- Primary metric: cost_per_request (stat test: two-sided t-test / bootstrap CI).
- Secondary metrics: model-quality-score, session-drop-rate, support_ticket_rate.
- Minimum detectable effect (MDE): estimate using historic variance; if MDE > expected lift, consider longer experiment or more users.

Measurement & analysis cadence:
- T+0h: sanity check — health metrics only. Post short slack update.
- T+4–6h: early metrics snapshot (latency, errors, cost). PM/Analyst review.
- T+24h: full metric run (pre-registered analysis, p-value/CI). SRE confirms no infra regressions.
- T+72h: operational stability review and business metrics check.

Communication templates (short):
- Slack start msg (to #prod-rollouts):
  "Rolling out canary: RI-1234, model v2 -> canary A (0.5%); owners @Aisha, @Miguel. Watching p95_latency, error_rate_5m, gpu_util. Will post T+30m."
- Slack hold msg:
  "Holding ramp on RI-1234: guardrail fired (p95 +25%). Reduced slice to 0.5%/previous stable. SRE investigating. Paging @oncall-sre."
- Slack rollback msg:
  "Rollback executed for RI-1234 at 15:43 UTC due to error spike. Reverted to v1. Incident ticket RI-1234-rollback created. Notifying stakeholders."

Runbook: immediate actions if guardrail triggers
- Step A (automated): Route engine reduces slice automatically per policy.
- Step B (Ops): SRE on-call checks logs, traces, and recent deploys; run flame graphs if CPU/GPU anomalies.
- Step C (Eng): Reproduce with same query set on staging; check model artifact integrity and kernel selection logs.
- Step D (PM): Pause marketing/CS communications; schedule a post-mortem if rollback.
- Step E (CS): If user-facing impact, load a quick FAQ + message template for customer contacts.

Coordination cadence (recommended for release sprint):
- Pre-launch 48h sync (30m): owners confirm QA, dashboards, safety nets.
- Launch day: 15m kickoff at handoff time. Assign live scribe.
- Post-launch daily: 10–15m standup for first 3 days (owners only).
- Retrospective: within one week; include ops timeline, root cause, and follow-ups.

Lightweight experiment hypothesis template (copy into ticket):
- Title: short descriptive name
- Owner: PM + Eng lead
- Start date / End date
- Audience: route(s)/cohorts
- Traffic split plan: detailed per-step percentages and durations
- Primary metric and measurement query (SQL/PromQL link)
- Safety metrics and guardrails + thresholds
- Rollback criteria & who can approve rollback
- Analysis plan: who runs stats and when

Notes to self / future improvements:
- We should add a templated dashboard in Console that wires up p95, error_rate, and cost for any rollout automatically.
- Add a simple canary traffic simulator used in PR checks to surface perf regressions early.
- Re-evaluate token_cost_per_1000 sensitivity: sometimes improved latency increases cost; need a cost+quality composite metric.

Links & references (internal):
- Runbook skeleton: confluence.redwood.ai/prod/rollouts-skeleton
- Canary config schema: github.com/redwood-inference/console/blob/main/docs/canary-schema.md
- Previous post-mortem: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=78901

TODOs (actionable):
- [ ] Add experiment template to ticket templates (owner: PM).
- [ ] Coordinate with SRE to create the auto-hold thresholds as standard policies (owner: SRE).
- [ ] Build one-click dashboard snapshot export for post-launch analysis (owner: Observability).

Endnotes: keep this doc lean. Copy, adapt, and paste into your experiment ticket. If a rollout is high-risk (PII, compliance scope, or enterprise SLA customer), switch to dedicated canary infra and shorten ramp thresholds.
